# M3.4: labeled synthetic sweep

Date: 2026-10-14. Detector `53a956583b6f` (model `iforest-acc0c2dc3985-seed7`, threshold 0.5811 at 25 alerts per 1,000 on calibration traffic, manifest `acc0c2dc3985`) against the `structural-rules-v1` rules. Reproduce with `blockpulse sweep` (see below). Local output: `data/sweeps/iforest-acc0c2dc3985-seed7-budget25-seed11/`.

**What this is.** 780 synthetic transactions with known shapes and labels, generated by this project (seed 11, 20 variants per cell). Transactions are internally consistent (input values equal outputs plus fee) and pass through the same feature function as real data. They test **how each detector responds to defined patterns**. They do not measure real-world detection accuracy or false-positive rates: the patterns and the "benign" controls are our own constructions, and none of it is real traffic.

## Run it

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m blockpulse sweep data/datasets/dataset-<id>.json data/models/iforest-<id>-seed7 data/evaluations/<evaluation dir>
```

It writes `cases.csv` (every case with labels and both detectors' decisions), `sweep.csv` (rates by family and severity), and `summary.json`. Synthetic cases are never part of training or calibration.

## Results by pattern

Flag rate = share of the 20 variants flagged. "Calibration percentile" is the median model score expressed as a position within the real calibration session's scores (0.98 = higher than 98% of those transactions).

| Pattern (size) | Rules | Model | Median calibration percentile |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| fan-out, 3 / 5 / 8 outputs | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.45 / 0.62 / 0.93 |
| fan-out, 10 / 15 / 20 outputs | 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.0 | 0 / 0.25 / 0.80 | 0.96 / 0.97 / 0.98 |
| fan-out, 50 / 100 / 300 outputs | 1.0 | 1.0 | 0.99+ |
| fan-in, 3 / 5 inputs | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 0.93 / 0.96 |
| fan-in, 8 / 10 / 15 inputs | 0 / 1.0 / 1.0 | 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.0 | 0.97 / 0.98 / 0.99 |
| fan-in, 20 to 300 inputs | 1.0 | 1.0 | 0.99+ |
| equal outputs, 2 / 3 / 5 | 0 / 1.0 / 1.0 | 0 / 0.2 / 1.0 | 0.96 / 0.97 / 0.98 |
| equal outputs, 10 / 20 / 50 | 1.0 | 1.0 | 0.99+ |
| fee rate 1 / 5 / 20 sat/vB | 0 | 0 | 0.35 / 0.35 / 0.53 |
| fee rate 100 / 500 / 2000 sat/vB | 0 | 0 | 0.94 / 0.95 / 0.95 |

Benign controls (20 variants each, expected to need no flag):

| Control | Rules | Model |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| ordinary payment | 0 | 0 |
| round-amount payment | 0 | 0 |
| high-fee payment (30 to 100 sat/vB) | 0 | 0 |
| small batch (2 inputs, 6 outputs) | 0 | 0 |
| small consolidation (4 inputs, 1 output) | 0 | 0 |
| large payment (0.1, 1, 10, 1,000 BTC total output) | 0 | 0.90 / 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.0 |

## What this shows

- **The rules do what they say.** All 780 cases produced exactly the rule IDs the label expects. This confirms the mechanics, not usefulness.
- **The rules are binary at a fixed shape threshold; the model is graded.** Rules flag every fan-out at 10 outputs or more and none below. The model's flag rate rises smoothly: fan-out of 10 outputs is flagged 0% of the time, 20 outputs 80%, 50 outputs 100%. At the same size it responds much more strongly to fan-in than fan-out (10 inputs: 80%; 10 outputs: 0%), because the training windows contain many more wide-output transactions, so wide outputs look more ordinary.
- **Fee outliers are invisible to both.** The rules have no fee rule. The model scores a 2,000 sat/vB fee about the same as 100 sat/vB (median score 0.50 against 0.50), and flags neither. The highest fee rate in the training data is 100, so the model cannot see beyond it: this is the "no extrapolation" limit in [the model note](../guides/06-ml-evaluation.md#2-the-model-isolation-forest), observed directly. An extreme fee rate is not necessarily suspicious, but a detector that would care about it needs a different mechanism.
- **The model flags a benign pattern the rules ignore.** It flags 78 of 80 large-payment controls (a single payment of 0.1 BTC or more with no other unusual structure), because large total output values are rare in the training windows. Large payments are ordinary behavior, so these count as false alarms *within this synthetic set*. The other five control families (100 cases) were never flagged by either detector.
- **Both detectors share one blind spot by construction.** Because they see only structure, a legitimate batch payout or consolidation has the same features as any other transaction with that shape, so neither detector can tell them apart (the existing rule lab demonstrates this).

## Limits

- Synthetic patterns reflect our assumptions about what a pattern looks like. Real transactions of the same shape have different value distributions, script types, and fee behavior.
- The model's flags depend on a threshold set from a single 10-minute calibration window and on a training set of about 30 minutes, so the flagging boundaries above (for example "fan-out of 20 outputs is flagged 80% of the time") will move as more sessions are added. Re-run the sweep after retraining.
- "Benign" here means "ordinary behavior we chose to generate", not verified benign real transactions.
- No claim about accuracy, precision or recall on real traffic follows from these results.
